facts.fact: The Civil Status Act, consolidated with amendments in force to 27 July 2024, has Civil Status Offices register births and deaths 'in any register or computer system' (s.3(1)(a)) and defines an entry as a manuscript entry in a register or an input on a computer system; it permits digital entry of both events and does not say which offices use it.
facts.system: Civil Status Database (CSD); computer system of the Civil Status Offices

facts.fact: Section 8A, in force from 1 September 2003, establishes a Civil Status Database of all entries registered under the Act and kept on a computer at the Central Civil Status Office, with the Registrar of Civil Status as its repository; the Civil Status Offices are under the Registrar's administrative control (s.3).

systems.tiers: kept on a computer at the Central Civil Status Office, holding all entries registered under the Act; Civil Status Offices register in a register or computer system; generates the NIC number

central; particulars of every person whose birth is registered in Mauritius or who becomes a citizen; access granted to ministries, departments and the Bank of Mauritius; s.8B in force 16 September 2013

systems.system: Registrar's electronic system for sharing information
systems.country_label: electronic system of the Registrar of Civil Status (s.17B)
systems.tiers: shares name, address, date of birth, NIC number, photograph and date of death with public sector agencies approved by the Minister; in force 15 February 2016

systems.owner: health ministry, private health institutions and midwives
systems.tiers: a prescribed form issued to the parents and the Registrar on a birth; inserted 2021 and marked not in operation; no electronic means stated

note: A later consolidation of the same Act as document 49, also an excerpt ending mid-section 22, before the Part on deaths. Not recorded as facts: how the record is made (a manuscript register or a computer input are both allowed, the parties sign the register, and outlying offices forward registers to the Central office at year end) and how many offices enter digitally, neither of which it states.
